components.name: Home discovery rail
components.description: Independent named rails beneath natural-language search. Existing ProductCards use real catalog photography at 168px/208px widths and 16px gaps; tracks reserve 352px/410px below/from 768px. Trending uses an 80px header; later headers use 112px on phones and 80px from 768px. Trending, preferences, history and friends have independent loading and retry states; both preference rails share one request. This preview shows the loading geometry. The implemented track supports touch, labelled 44px paging buttons, Arrow keys, Home/End and reduced-motion paging.

narrative.overview: Lookline is a well-lit store: a white wall, one steel rail, paper tags. The garment is the only colour on the page; the interface is the rail and the tags. The largest element on every screen is a piece of clothing or a Look, the one ink button is the next step in the chain, and text is a caption, never a paragraph.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-neutral white wall with white paper tags and a recessed panel tone
Ink for every primary action; tag red for the one thing that needs attention
One-pixel rail lines separate groups; borders are for tags and inputs
Image-first tiles that lift off the rail on hover — the only shadow
Rails for curated sets, grids for catalogs
Engine internals behind the Engine view switch, never on consumer pages

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: Product artwork and Look images supply the page's colour; the interface stays neutral so they can.

rules.name: The Tag Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks a single consequential thing per screen. If two things are red, one of them is not.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Text under an image is a caption: name, price, one reason. Sentence case, no tracked uppercase, no kickers above headings.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque names pages and Looks; Inter operates. Never the reverse.

rules.name: The First Viewport Rule
rules.body: On every page the largest thing above the fold is an image; on Find it is the input sitting over a rail of real garments. Controls never push content below the fold on a 390px screen.

rules.name: The Rail-or-Grid Rule
rules.body: Curated sets hang on rails; catalogs stand in grids. Never a stack of same-size cards.

rules.name: The One Reason Rule
rules.body: A recommendation carries one plain line from its strongest factors; scores, weights, confidence and breakdowns exist only in Engine view.

rules.name: The Honest State Rule
rules.body: Loading, unavailable, empty, error, rendering and sample states are visible and distinct, expressed as form rather than prose.

rules.name: The Shop Talk Direct Update Rule
rules.body: On `/shop-talk`, conversation replaces the sentence field, hints and apply controls. Assistant filter updates act directly on the catalog; manual changes remain visible in the transcript. Google Search only helps interpret unfamiliar named references; product discovery stays in the site's Jev/catalog flow, without external search results, suggestion cards or source links. Uncertain preferences remain conversational and do not trigger alerts. Actual service failures retain retry or reconnect actions; an unavailable catalog remains distinct from a successful search with no matches.

dos: Do open every page on an image and end it on the one ink button.
Do write like a good clerk: name the outcome, keep the rest to a line.
Do put engine internals behind Engine view and in the Engine lab.
Do hang curated sets on rails and let them bleed to the phone's edge.
Do label sample states with a small "Sample" tag.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, or a slogan in a title.
Don't narrate the system or explain what a button does.
Don't show scores, percentages, confidence or field names to a shopper.
Don't nest cards, border layout groups, or list aesthetic chips under a product.
Don't use red for anything that is not the one thing to notice.
